channel.description: Recent content in Experiments on Joulie

item.title: CPU-Only Benchmark
item.description: These results come from the Joulie simulator, Joulie’s test bed for its behaviour (caps applied, placement, policies), not evidence of energy savings. Their energy figures rest on hardware behaviour the simulator assumes: every CPU core does the same work per second whatever its model, and cap responses, power curves and workload intensities are assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes. They do not show what Joulie saves on real hardware; what meaningful experiments need is tracked in the milestone Evidence-based evaluation.

item.title: Governor Exploration
item.description:
This page reports experiment 05, CPU and GPU governor presets as an energy dimension of their own, next to power caps:

  • experiments/05-governor-exploration/

Joulie writes a governor as a vendor-neutral preset in the NodeTwin (spec.cpu.governor.preset: performance, balanced, efficiency; spec.gpu.governor.preset: auto, sustained, efficient, low, peak), and the agent maps it to the native words of the node’s CPU frequency driver and GPU family. Governor control is off by default (GOVERNOR_CONTROL, GOVERNOR_WRITES, Configuration reference).

item.title: Scoring Formula Validation
item.description: Not a valid result. An audit of this experiment found that jobs that do not fit are dropped instead of queued, and energy is divided by the placed jobs only; the arms are mislabelled, and the selected formula never ran through the cooling model; the formula was chosen and reported on the same 8 seeds. The scripts model the cluster, the cooling and the scheduler’s formula in Python and import no Joulie code, so they do not follow changes to the extender. Its results do not stand and are not published. The experiment is to be redone on the scheduling logic extracted into an importable library (#122), as a behaviour scenario (#115).
